review: The Arabic prints the first stanza as three lines (the refrain, then two long lines); Hebrew keeps the same 3-line shape so the payload matches the printed book.

3:1 נִמְחָה עַל־הַצְּלָב — the Arabic has 'it wiped at the cross' with the subject in line 2; Hebrew fronts the verb and leaves the subject (דַּם אֲדֹנִי) for the next line, as the tune's caesura requires.

3:3–3:4 — 'from my gloomy heart all care has gone'; the Arabic puts הַמّ (care) at the head of 3:4, Hebrew at the end, to keep the rhyme of 3:2/3:4 (חֶטְאִי / דְּאָגָה is a near-rhyme only; the tune does not demand a true rhyme here).
4:4 כֹּפֶר לַחַיָּב — 'a ransom for the guilty'; כֹּפֶר is the biblical ransom (Ex 21:30) and the line is the doctrinal centre of the stanza.
